The source explicitly identifies pyopneumo- as a composite for pus and gas. Reverso analyses pyopneumothorax as pyo- pus plus pneumo- air plus thorax; the 2022 independent English medical paper attests the exact term for pus and air in the pleural cavity. The root groups the adjacent pyo and pneumo elements; it is not claimed to be a single indivisible historical morpheme.

The Oslo university hospital explicitly explains mandibulo as lower jaw and facial as face; NIH-hosted medical literature independently uses mandibulofacial dysostosis. MW documents the mandibulo- combining form. The previously unverified mandibulopharyngeal example is not included.

Two independent word references explicitly analyze rhombohedron as rhombo- plus -hedron. Rhombo here refers to a rhombus; the existing related rhomb form includes rhombus. The unresolved rhombencephalon is not used.

The independent Collins dictionary explicitly segments syringomyelia as syringo- plus -myelia; the medical history study independently describes the component as tube-shaped and the other as spinal cord. This belongs to the already recorded syring pipe family.
The University of New Hampshire explicitly divides the living genus Ceratophyllum into cerato- horn and -phyllum leaf. This confirms the horn sense without the ambiguous o of Ceratodus.
The independent dictionary article identifies cerco- as tailed and -pithecus as monkey in the living Cercopithecus group. Its one typo is distinct from the separately recorded genus name.
The international anatomical terminology reference explicitly labels cerebello as the cerebellum prefix and pontine as the pons-derived adjective for the cerebellopontine cistern.
The independent dictionary explicitly analyzes homocercal as homo- plus cercal; the source records -cercal with the exact word. It denotes a fish-tail type.

entries.meaning: tail formation of a specified kind
entries.reason: The independent affix dictionary explicitly lists heterocercy under -cercy; the source independently identifies -cercy as a tail-formation ending.
MW identifies ilio- as the iliac combining form; Collins independently lists iliofemoral under ilio-. Its ilium sense is anatomically distinct from ileo- for the small intestine.
MW explicitly associates infero- below with inferolateral; the university hospital medical dictionary independently divides inferolateral into infero- below plus lateral.
MW records ischio- for the ischium; Taber independently and explicitly divides ischiofemoral into ischio- plus femoral, relating the ischium to the femur.

MW records jejuno- for jejunum and jejunal compounds. NIH MeSH independently uses jejunoileal for a bypass connecting the jejunum and ileum. This selects a compound with a clear jejuno plus ileal boundary rather than the competing -ostomy segmentation of jejunostomy.

entries.meaning: mercapto group; derived from a mercaptan
entries.reason: MW identifies mercapto- as related to mercaptans; the independent Britannica reference hosted by the US Patent Office explicitly identifies mercapto- as the sulfur-containing group and uses 2-mercaptoethanol as an example. NIH MeSH independently names mercaptoethanol as a thiol derived from ethanol.

MW identifies mnemo- with memory and mnemotechnical; the independent dictionary explicitly analyses mnemotechnic as mnemo- plus technic. The exact English adjective is selected, avoiding the shorter-form overlap question.

American Heritage identifies oxaloacetate as a name combining oxalic and acetic acid; Wiktionary gives oxalo- plus acetate. MW records oxalo- as related to oxalic acid. The assignment describes the naming relation, not an assertion that the compound is free oxalic acid.

Collins explicitly derives tocopherol from toco- offspring or childbirth, a bearing element, and -ol; the university nutrition text separately explains the Greek naming history. This is a historical naming connection, not a claim that the vitamin treats fertility conditions.

The independent 1924 dictionary identifies chyli- as a combining form for chyle, gives chyliferous as chyle plus -ferous, and shows the full i belongs before -ferous. Quebec terminology defines the current English term chyliferous vessel. Unlike chyliform, no -iform boundary is involved.

The dictionary explicitly splits embolotherapy into embolo- plus therapy. The US National Library of Medicine independently records embolotherapy as therapeutic embolization, so the o is part of the exact combining form.

MW explicitly identifies ependymo- with ependyma. Gene Ontology independently records ependymocyte as an ependymal cell, and another dictionary analyzes ependymo- plus -cyte. The source example ependymoepithelium remains unaccepted.

LPSN explicitly segments the currently valid bacterial genus Fusibacter as Fusi plus bacter and traces it to Latin fusus spindle. The original taxonomic publication independently describes the spindle-shaped genus. This avoids the ambiguous -iform boundary in fusiform.

MW records dein- and deino- as fearsome; the independent dictionary explicitly derives the dinosaur genus Deinonychus from Greek dein meaning terrible plus -onychos clawed. The initial bare dein form ends before the o in the independently attested -onychos element.

entries.meaning: having a specified kind of skin
entries.reason: MW explicitly lists -dermatous with sclerodermatous; the independently maintained suffix entry lists the same word, and the European Medicines Agency uses the adjective for affected skin areas in a current medical report.

The International Code of Zoological Nomenclature specifies -ini for animal tribes. The university zoology taxonomy reference independently lists Bombini as a tribe with the suffix -ini; this is a current specialist scientific taxon.

MW records larvi- for larvae; the USDA and FAO independently define larviculture as cultivating larvae. The larvi + culture analysis is an inference from the documented form and meaning, and avoids an -iform or -igerous boundary. The linked larv family traces its historical sense to mask or ghost.

MW records lati- for wide; the independent roots reference explicitly assigns lati to latifundium and Latin fundus estate. This historically documented Latin compound belongs to the wide sense, not the other lat families meaning side or carry.

MW records lamelli- for a lamella; the independent dictionary traces lamellibranch to the name Lamellibranchia and explicitly points to lamelli- and -branch. This English noun refers to a bivalve; the historical subclass name should not be promoted as a current classification.

MW explicitly lists kinesimeter for kinesi- motion; the independent Wiktionary entry explicitly divides it into kinesi- and -meter, while the independent technical dictionary lists the exact English headword. This avoids the kinesio plus -logy ambiguity of kinesiology.
MW documents pelago- for the sea, and the independent dictionary explicitly derives pelagobenthic from pelago- plus benthic. The earlier uncertain pelagophyte is not assigned.

American Heritage explicitly gives pollini- and the example polliniferous; MW independently lists the same form and word. The existing pollin family preserves its older fine-flour gloss, while this form is restricted to pollen.

MW records lymphato- for lymphatic tissue. A 2024 surgical article independently uses lymphatovenous for an anastomosis in the lymphatic and venous system; the link to the combining form is an inference from the documented form and context, not a claimed direct dictionary decomposition.

entries.reason: MW records cole- and coleo- as sheath variants and lists coleorhiza; the University of Kansas botanical terminology resource independently lists coleo- (cole-) for sheath with this example. entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW records coccygeo- for coccygeal and; the independently peer-reviewed anatomy atlas defines a coccygeofemoral muscle slip as arising from the coccyx and attaching to the femur. The combination is inferred from the attested form and anatomical description.

entries.reason: MW records condylo- for a joint or condyle. The independent dictionary explicitly analyzes condylotomy as condylo- plus -tomy. Current medical usage is independently documented at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35397232/.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW records cotylo- for cup-shaped organs and the acetabular sense. The independent orthopedic paper explicitly uses cotyloplasty for acetabular reconstruction. The boundary cotylo- plus -plasty is a morphology inference supported by the named operation, not a quoted dictionary parsing.

entries.meaning: creature with specified leg or shin
entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW explicitly lists the animal genus Octacnemus under -cnemus, legged or shinned. SeaLifeBase independently lists it as a living genus with species. This does not claim a precise anatomical equivalence between its lobes and legs or an independent derivation by SeaLifeBase.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW explicitly records the hair-related suffix -coma with Pycnocoma. Kew independently confirms Pycnocoma is an accepted plant genus; this historical naming element is unrelated to the medical condition coma.

MW records kerauno- for thunder; King’s College London independently explicitly explains kerauno meaning lightning in keraunophobia, and Wiktionary explicitly segments the English term into kerauno- plus -phobia. It is related to existing cerauno by transliteration.

MW records -dectes as biter in animal genus names. The independent peer-reviewed publication formally names the fossil genus Alveusdectes and expressly derives the suffix dectes as biter. Placement of the fossil group has been debated, but the genus and word formation are documented.

entries.meaning: speech; a specified condition of speech
entries.reason: Oxford psychology dictionary explicitly analyses alogia as a- without plus logia words; Wiktionary explicitly lists alogia as an English example under -logia for speech conditions. The speech sense is separated from the unrelated study-of mapping.

MW explicitly lists Luso- Portuguese and Luso-Brazilian. Cambridge University Press independently uses Luso-Brazilian for the Portuguese-Brazilian historical world; a current Penn Library article applies it to cultural materials.

The IMA list establishes manganochromite as an approved mineral with manganese and chromium. The mineral database independently explains its name from manganese and chromite, avoiding the superseded manganocolumbite example.

LPSN explicitly divides the validly published genus Mastigocladus into Mastigo plus cladus, meaning whip-like branch. The source records mastigo- as whip; this replaces the outdated Mastigophora taxon.

The source explicitly records mathematico- for mathematical-and. An English-language philosophy paper independently uses mathematico-physical for facts concerning mathematics and physics, and a university curriculum uses the exact hyphenated adjective.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW records gravito- as relating to gravity. The independent physics review uses gravitomagnetic for effects of gravitational fields, analogous to magnetic effects. The specific combination gravito- plus magnetic is an inference from the verified form and technical use.

entries.reason: MW explicitly lists gloeo- sticky with Gloeocapsa; the independent bacterial nomenclature authority explicitly analyzes the valid genus name as Gloeo plus capsa, a sticky box.

entries.reason: MW identifies gonidio- as a form for gonidium; the independent scientific dictionary derives gonidiophore from gonidium and Greek pherein bearing. A contemporary cell-biology glossary separately attests the exact English word.

entries.reason: MW explicitly associates hadro- thick with Hadrosaurus. London Natural History Museum independently explains the dinosaur genus name as bulky lizard and retains the genus in its dinosaur directory.

entries.reason: MW identifies hapto- with contact or combination. An independent biochemical chapter explicitly analyzes haptoglobin as hapto for binding plus globin; the serum protein is named for its binding of hemoglobin.

MW explicitly identifies myi- as the short fly form and myio- as a longer variant. The independent Canadian Botanical Association article uses myiophilous and explains myio as fly. Connecting the shorter myi form to the same word is a documented-variant inference, with o belonging to the longer myio form and philous starting at ph; it does not rely on the ambiguous Myiarchus boundary.
MW records myio- as fly. The Canadian Botanical Association independently uses myiophilous for fly-pollinated and explicitly identifies myio as fly, distinguishing it from myo meaning mouse.

MW explicitly lists myelino- and myelinogenesis; an independent contemporary peer-reviewed review uses myelinogenesis for myelin formation, and a medical dictionary traces it to myelin plus genesis. An independent history paper traces myelin to Greek myelos marrow; the family link preserves the specific myelin sense rather than reassigning marrow examples.

MW records nanno- as dwarf; the University of New Hampshire explicitly derives the microalgal genus Nannochloropsis from nanno small and chloropsis green. A separate published research paper confirms nanno denotes very small in the genus name. This is the size sense, distinct from the SI prefix nano meaning one billionth.

MW records the suffix -myia for fly with Anthomyia; the independent dictionary explicitly derives the currently used fly genus from Greek anthos flower and myia fly. The older NIH-hosted text independently records the exact name and derivation; it is not being used as a source of current disease guidance.

MW explicitly lists -mimus as imitator with Cetomimus; ETYFish independently explains the current whalefish genus name as ceto whale plus mimus actor, referring to its whale-like appearance. FishBase independently records the same etymological elements.

entries.meaning: oxygen replacing carbon in a ring
entries.reason: PubChem lists oxacyclohexane and identifies this structure as cyclohexane with one carbon replaced by oxygen; NIST independently records the same exact chemical name. This is the replacement-prefix sense, not any unrelated oxa substring.

The marine dictionary explicitly lists ostrei- for oysters alongside ostreiculture, and an ICES fisheries report independently uses ostreiculture for oyster farming. This avoids the previous -iform boundary ambiguity.

An independent English-language report defines ostreophagous as feeding on oysters; the Indian government English-Urdu dictionary lists both ostreo- for oyster and ostreophagous. The source confirms the exact combining-form sense.

The source identifies pallio- for pallium and pallial relations. An independent neuroscience paper describes palliostriatal projections from pallium to striatum; another scientific review defines neural pallium. This is an inference from attested morphology and subject matter, not a claimed explicit dictionary split.

MW records muci- for mucus; the independent dictionary explicitly parses mucigel as muci- plus gel, the University of Oslo describes the slimy root matrix, and a modern university research case uses the term. The example avoids the competing -iform and -iferous boundaries.

entries.meaning: eater; organism feeding in a specified way
entries.reason: MW explicitly lists -phagus with the animal genus Melophagus. Treccani independently derives the genus as Greek sheep plus -phagus eater, and LPSN explicitly shows Melo plus phagus.
MW and the independent Random House dictionary explicitly list hydrophily under -phily for affinity. The independent biology publication uses hydrophily in the specific sense of water pollination.
An EU regional research report explicitly traces paludi to Latin palus swamp in paludiculture, and UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology defines the current word as wetland farming.

Etymonline explicitly identifies party-colored as a variant referring to colors in different parts, and Dictionary.com records this English spelling as a variant of parti-colored. This is the color sense, not a political party.

Taber explicitly lists parvi- as small and parvicellular as a variant of parvocellular; UC San Diego describes the parvicellular region as a group of small cells. This combines a verified form with an attested word rather than claiming the second source directly segments it.

An independent historical scientific dictionary derives pectinibranchiate from Latin pecten comb plus branchiate; McGraw-Hill uses pectinibranch for a comb-like mollusk gill. This is a gill-description word, not the obsolete Pectinibranchia group.
MW records Serbo- for Serbian and related compounds. UCLA and the Canadian language portal independently use Serbo-Croatian, while noting distinct contemporary language standards.

MW explicitly lists serpenti- and serpentivorous. The independent word-element reference lists serpenti- with the same word, and Wiktionary independently records the English adjective for eating snakes.
The source gives Siculo- for Sicilian. Modern historical-linguistics work at Sapienza University and a Library of Congress collection independently use Siculo-Arabic for a language variety in Sicily.

The source identifies Sinico- for Chinese and. Independent linguistics papers use Sinico-Japanese for a written style combining Chinese and Japanese conventions; it is a specialized hyphenated descriptor.

A historical English dictionary explicitly lists sorediferous as a word built with soredi- for soredium; the Consortium of Lichen Herbaria independently uses sorediferous in a current species description.

entries.reason: The Australian Government Flora of Australia explicitly derives the plant genus name Hedychium from Greek hedys sweet and chion snow. North Carolina State University separately confirms the genus is in use.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW directly gives heredofamilial as an example of heredo- relating to heredity. The independent official Quebec terminology database records the English term as a synonym of hereditary.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW defines humero- as humeral and; the independent anatomy reference identifies the humeroradial joint as an anatomical structure. Segmentation into humero- and radial is an inference from the dictionary form and anatomical use.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW identifies hydat- and hydato- as related water forms. An independent dictionary analyzes hydatophyte as hydato- plus -phyte, and a contemporary scientific journal attests the English word. Hydat- is the documented shorter related stem; no unique segmentation is claimed.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW identifies hydato- as a form meaning water. An independent dictionary explicitly analyzes hydatophyte as hydato- plus -phyte, and a contemporary scientific journal attests the English word.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: Collins explicitly analyzes the English adjective hyetal as hyet- plus -al and defines it as relating to rain. The Canadian government terminology bank independently attests the word while labeling it rare.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: The International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants explicitly specifies notho- for hybrid taxa and uses the term nothospecies. MW independently records notho- as a related combining form.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW gives the animal genus Camponotus as an example of -notus having a specified back. An Auburn University dissertation independently explains the genus name as campo bent plus notum back; a USDA publication confirms current use of the ant genus.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: The independent Greek and Latin affixes dictionary lists novo- new and novobiocin together. Health Canada uses novobiocin in a current pathogen safety data sheet; MW independently records novo- meaning new.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW explicitly gives occlusogingival as an example of occluso- occlusal and. The independent Leeds dental thesis uses the term for a dimension between occlusal and gingival landmarks; the precise segmentation is an inference from those sources.

MW explicitly lists phoro- carrying or motion with phorozooid; Wiktionary independently segments phorozooid into phoro- and zooid. The peer-reviewed marine biology review describes phorozooids carrying developing gonozooids.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: The independent Dictionary of Medical Terms explicitly records oesophago- for oesophagus and oesophagojejunostomy as a surgical connection between the esophagus and jejunum. The proposed oesophago- plus jejunostomy segmentation is an inference.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW groups onch- and oncho- as hook forms. The University of Kentucky independently derives the currently used parasite genus Onchocerca from Greek onkos hook and kerkos tail; the shorter onch- is a documented variant, not a claim of unique segmentation.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW groups onch- and oncho- as hook forms. The University of Kentucky independently derives the currently used parasite genus Onchocerca from Greek onkos hook and kerkos tail. A separate same-spelling tumor sense is not included in this decision.

entries.origin: Greek or Latin; see reviewed source
entries.reason: MW defines opsono- as relating to opsonin; an independent dictionary explicitly analyzes opsonophagocytosis as opsono- plus phagocytosis. A peer-reviewed medical paper separately uses the current English term.

MW and Masaryk University medical terminology notes give -stasia and the example astasia. A 2023 clinical report independently uses astasia for inability to maintain standing, matching the standing sense.

The independent word-element reference places the English variant dyscinesia under -cinesia for movement. Both Quebec and Canadian government terminology services record dyscinesia as an English alternative to dyskinesia. The exact c spelling is verified, and belongs to the existing -kinesia family.

ITIS identifies Tetracerus as a valid extant antelope genus and Tetraceros as an invalid emendation. An independent peer-reviewed mammalogy article derives Tetracerus from Greek four plus horn. MW lists the suffix with that spelling but confusingly describes it as an insect genus; this decision uses independently documented mammal usage, not that taxonomic claim.

MW records spiri- as a coil form. The Austrian geological collection explicitly derives fossil genus Spirifer from Latin spira coil and fero bear; Yale Peabody specimen records identify Spirifer as an accepted taxon. This coiling sense is separate from existing spir meaning breathe.

MW records classico- for classical and; an independent contemporary musical review and Boston University historical collection use classico-romantic for classical and Romantic musical traditions. The exact hyphen makes the compound boundary explicit.

MW records taenio- for tapeworm, Taber independently indexes taeniophobia, and the independent word-elements source groups the precise English term under taenio for tapeworm. This acceptance is restricted to the tapeworm sense.

MW explicitly records telluro- for tellurium and the example tellurobismuthite. The independent mineral database traces its name to tellurium and bismuth, and the Italian heritage mineral list records it as an IMA species.
MW explicitly lists termito- termite and termitophagous. Independent peer-reviewed zoological work uses the adjective for termite-eating organisms and explains termitophagy as termite eating.
MW records tetano- for tetanus; the independent historical dictionary explicitly links tetanospasmin to that form, and a modern peer-reviewed review uses the exact term for tetanus toxin.

MW documents tyl- and tylo- together for knob and lists Tylosaurus. Cambridge University Press independently derives the recognized fossil genus from Greek tylos projection and sauros lizard; the short form is a documented variant with connecting o.
MW lists tylo- and Tylosaurus; Cambridge University Press independently derives the fossil genus from tylos projection plus sauros lizard, and the Missouri Botanical Garden describes tylo- as knob.
MW records umbelli- for an umbel; Collins explicitly derives umbelliferous using umbelli- plus -fer and -ous, independently establishing the i boundary.

entries.meaning: animal or group having a specified tail
entries.reason: MW explicitly lists -ura with Brachyura; the Natural History Museum independently explains the currently used crab grouping name as short-tailed and PubChem confirms that taxonomic use.
MW explicitly lists -urus with Dasyurus; American Heritage and the independent Australian fauna reference explain the living quoll genus name as Greek hairy plus tail.
MW records vario- for varied; both American Heritage and an independent etymological reference explicitly list variometer under vario- for variation.

MW records cyath- as a cup form; the University of Florida explains that the current fungal genus Cyathus means cup, and the independent mycological reference explicitly traces the genus name to Greek kyath- cup. This is the short form with Latin -us, not the disputed cyathiform suffix boundary.

MW identifies -ineae as an ending for plant suborders. The botanical nomenclature code explicitly uses the ending -ineae and gives Malvineae as its example; a university teaching reference independently confirms the suborder suffix. This establishes nomenclatural formation and does not assert current taxonomic rank.

MW explicitly lists intermedio- and intermediolateral. The independent English dictionary directly divides intermediolateral into intermedio- and lateral; the NIH neuroanatomy reference independently uses the word for the spinal column.

ETYFish explicitly analyses the fish subgenus Sebastosomus as Sebastes plus somus, body; it treats the name’s precise allusion to body shape as an unconfirmed conjecture. A 2022 peer-reviewed fish study uses Sebastosomus as a subgenus. The suffix is provisionally associated with the existing som body family; other homonymous families are not automatically merged.

The 1924 dictionary explicitly analyzes lalophobia as lalo- plus -phobia, and an independent current English dictionary attests it for fear of speaking. MW records lalo- as speech. The relation is lexical and does not imply a current psychiatric diagnosis.

MW records lecitho- as egg yolk; the University of Portsmouth explicitly describes lecithotrophic larvae as deriving nutrition from egg yolk, and an independent peer-reviewed paper uses the same term in this meaning. The form-to-word decomposition is an inference from a documented form and matching usage; the unrelated lecithoprotein example is not used.

MW explicitly groups melam- with the black form melan- and lists the fungus genus Melampsora. Two independent scientific references trace the genus to Greek melas black and psora scab; the spelling melam- represents the corresponding nasal variant before p.

MW identifies -meryx for ruminants, especially extinct genera. The peer-reviewed 2021 paper formally names Krabimeryx and explicitly explains meryx as Greek for ruminant; an independent paleontology paper confirms the same suffix sense.

Collins records serriform as a biology term meaning sawlike and explicitly analyzes it as serri- (Latin serra, saw) plus -form. This directly resolves the earlier uncertainty about whether i belongs only to -iform.

Merriam-Webster directly lists palmi- in the sense of palm of the hand with example palmigrade; independent primate anatomy research describes palmigrade locomotion as hand posture in which the palm contacts the ground. This uses the hand sense rather than the separate palm-tree sense.

Merriam-Webster lists speciogenesis under specio- meaning species. The 2018 Torre-Bueno Glossary of Entomology independently treats speciogenesis as a synonym of speciation, the origin or multiplication of species.

Merriam-Webster assigns faradotherapy to farado- in the sense of faradic stimulation. A medical-translation journal records the English term, and a medical dictionary defines it as treatment using faradic induced current. This confirms the term and relation, not that this treatment is currently recommended.

Merriam-Webster explicitly lists pennoplume for penno- feather. An independent word-element reference defines English pennoplume as a feather or semiplume; a dictionary source explains pennoplume as penno- plus plume. The term is specialized, and no claim is made that it is common in current ornithology.

Merriam-Webster includes choristoblastoma in the choristo- entry. An independent medical article explains its Greek components choristos separated, blastos germ and oma tumor, and a medical dictionary records the exact English spelling and sense. Unlike choristoma, the chosen word does not depend on sharing the o with -oma.
